Antarctica is calling: Applications open for Scott Base crew 2026/27

About 40 jobs are on offer for those willing to brave sub-zero temperatures and work in one of the most remote places on earth.

Antarctica New Zealand has launched a nation‑wide recruitment drive, inviting people across Aotearoa to work at Scott Base in Antarctica for the 2026/27 research season.

New Zealand’s small but mighty research station needs maintenance engineers, field staff, carpenters, chefs, mechanics, electricians, medics and technicians to keep Scott Base running and support the scientists working on the ice.

Most roles will run from September through to February, though some positions will require applicants to embrace the challenge of working through an Antarctic winter, where sub-freezing temperatures can dip as low as minus 50 degrees.

Scott Base exists so scientists can uncover how our planet is changing—it has served as New Zealand’s permanent Antarctic research station since 1957.

Answer the call: www.anatarcticanz.govt.nz/careers

Applications close on 15 March 2026.

Successful applicants will receive comprehensive training, with food and accommodation also provided. Candidates must be eligible to work in New Zealand.

CRL Tunnel Vision February 2026

Tēnā koe,

Antony Ruru (Te Aitanga-a-Mahaki, Ngāti Porou) | EIT Bachelor of Arts (Māori) Graduate

From hesitation at the door to life changing learning, Antony Ruru’s (Te Aitanga-a-Mahaki, Ngāti Porou) journey into Te Reo Māori at EIT. 

We’re excited to share this heartfelt kōrero from Bachelor of Arts (Māori) graduate, Antony Ruru.

In this video, Anthony reflects on the moment that changed everything, sitting in his car outside EIT, unsure if he was ready to take that next step. After three attempts at reaching for the door, it was a warm “Kia ora, do you want to come in?” from staff member Ange that finally welcomed him inside and set him on a new path.

Growing up in Tairāwhiti with his mum and grandmother speaking Te Reo at home, to enrolling in Te Whakangungutanga ki Ngā Tāiro a Kupe | Bachelor of Arts (Māori), Anthony describes his study journey as one of the best experiences of his life. A journey that helped him reconnect with te ao Māori, strengthen his identity, and grow in ways he never expected.

If you’re thinking about studying Te Reo, reconnecting with your culture, or taking a step you’re not quite sure you’re ready for, Antony’s story shows just how transformative that first “yes” can be.

How to identify and remove Moth Plant

Have you got moth plant on your property and want to remove it?

In this video, our Senior Biosecurity Advisor Warren Pegley, breaks down what moth plant looks like, why it’s a problem in Napier and Hastings urban areas, and the simple things you can do to help slow it down, especially before it starts producing big pods packed with fluffy seeds that can blow long distances.

You’ll learn to easily identify moth plant, plus practical and safe removal tips you can use on your property.

If you’ve ever wondered why Regional Council isn’t tackling every plant in town, Warren explains why the focus is on containing spread outside urban centres and why community action on properties and along fence lines really does make a difference.

Learn more about moth plant on our Pest Hub. Visit: https://www.hbrc.govt.nz/environment/pest-control/pest-hub/pests/pest/107?family=15

How to identify Senegal Tea

Senegal tea is a fast-growing, semi-aquatic plant that can quickly dominate water bodies by forming dense floating mats of stems which displace and outcompete native aquatic vegetation. Distinctive white, clover-like flowers appear from November through to April.

For more info on Senegal tea or visit: https://hbrc.info/senegaltea

Reporting it? https://hbrc.info/pestreporting

Join Health New Zealand's Procurement team

Discover what a career in procurement looks like at Health New Zealand. In this video, we follow one of our procurement specialists whose journey began in nursing and aviation before moving into large-scale national health projects — including leading a billion-dollar helicopter services contract.

Health procurement is complex, fast-paced and deeply rewarding. From aeromedical services to radiotherapy machines, mattresses and patient beds, our teams help deliver the equipment and services that keep hospitals running and support care for communities across Aotearoa New Zealand.

Hear firsthand how strong partnerships, strategic procurement, and meaningful work come together to make a real difference for patients every day.

If you're looking for a career with purpose, impact and growth, join us at Health New Zealand.

Why I moved: A UK GP’s journey to New Zealand General Practice — Luke's Story

Discover why Dr. Luke Bradford and his family fell in love with New Zealand’s lifestyle and never looked back. From working as house officers in local hospitals to owning a successful urban practice and serving as President of the Royal New Zealand College of GPs, Luke’s journey showcases the incredible career growth and outdoor lifestyle available to medical professionals in Aotearoa.

In this video, you’ll explore:

1. A Fulfilling Career Path: Luke shares his journey from house officer to practice owner and his leadership role at the Royal New Zealand College of GPs.

2. Urban GP Practice Insights: Learn about working in a large urban practice like Fifth Avenue Family Practice, managing chronic diseases, and performing minor surgeries.

3. The "NZ Advantage" in Medicine: Why GPs in New Zealand have more autonomy and direct patient management compared to other countries.

4. Ultimate Work-Life Balance: From skiing and fishing to kayaking and hiking the length of New Zealand (Te Araroa trail), discover how Luke balances professional excellence with personal passion.

5. Raising a Family in Paradise: Why New Zealand is the perfect place to raise active, outdoorsy kids and build lifelong memories.

6. Advice for International Doctors: Luke’s top tips for doctors considering a move and why you definitely won’t regret making the leap.

Why Practice General Practice in Tauranga?
Tauranga offers the perfect blend of urban convenience and stunning natural beauty. Whether you’re interested in clinical leadership, specialized medical care, or simply want more time for the things you love, New Zealand provides a professional and personal environment that is hard to beat.

Learn more about GP careers in New Zealand: https://info.health.nz/careers/roles/senior-medical-officers/general-practitioners-rural-hospital-doctors

#GPJobs #NewZealandHealthcare #WorkInNZ #Tauranga #DoctorLife #HealthNZ #GeneralPractice #Aotearoa #MedicalRecruitment #InternationalDoctors #WorkLifeBalance #TeAraroa #GPProfessionals

Work life balance as a GP in Aotearoa New Zealand — Jenny's Story

Are you looking for a medical career that offers true work-life balance in one of the world's most stunning locations? Join Dr. Jenny as she explores her life as a General Practitioner (GP) in Wellington, the coastal capital of Aotearoa New Zealand.

From fulfilling work in refugee medicine to afternoon surf sessions, Jenny highlights the flexibility and professional satisfaction that comes with practicing medicine in the New Zealand healthcare system.

In this video, you’ll discover:

1. Meaningful Clinical Diversity: Jenny discusses her rewarding role at a not-for-profit clinic specializing in refugee medicine and her work in student health.

2. The GP Training Pathway: Gain insight into the three-year GP Education Programme, which balances formal seminars with supervised clinical practice.

3. A Supportive Work Culture: Hear why the New Zealand medical environment is more relaxed, making practitioners feel truly valued.

4. Unbeatable Lifestyle & Family Time: See how flexible hours allow Jenny to balance her career with raising a family and enjoying New Zealand's "great outdoors"—including surfing, swimming with dolphins, and coastal running.

5. Guidance for International Professionals: Jenny explains why the move is easier than you think and why you might just end up staying forever.

Why Practice General Practice in NZ?
Choosing a GP career in New Zealand means joining a system that prioritizes mental well-being and community connection. Whether you are drawn to the vibrant culture of Wellington or the flexible "choose your own hours" approach to medicine, New Zealand offers a lifestyle that is both fulfilling and sustainable.

Learn more about healthcare careers in New Zealand: https://info.health.nz/careers/roles/senior-medical-officers/general-practitioners-rural-hospital-doctors

#GPJobs #NewZealandHealthcare #WorkInNZ #Wellington #DoctorLife #HealthNZ #GeneralPractice #Aotearoa #MedicalRecruitment #InternationalDoctors #WorkLifeBalance

A day in the life of a rural GP in Aotearoa New Zealand – Andrew's story

Ever wondered what it’s like to practice medicine in one of the most beautiful places on Earth? Join Dr. Andrew as he shares his journey of moving from the UK to become a General Practitioner (GP) in Wanaka, New Zealand.

From treating ski slope injuries to balancing a fulfilling clinical career with a world-class outdoor lifestyle, Andrew explains why making the move to rural medicine in New Zealand was "totally worth it."

In this video, you’ll discover:

1. A Unique Clinical Variety: Learn about the "acute" nature of rural practice, including broken bones, lacerations, and farm-related injuries that differ from urban settings.

2. Work-Life Balance: How Andrew balances his GP duties and mental health advisory role with trail running, biking, skiing, and kayaking.

3. Moving to New Zealand with Family: Andrew shares his experience relocating from the UK and how his young family quickly settled into the Wānaka community.

4. Advice for Overseas Doctors: Why you should consider the move and the incredible cultural and geographical variety available to healthcare professionals in Aotearoa, New Zealand.

Why Choose Rural GP Practice in NZ?
Working as a GP in a rural community like Wānaka offers a level of fulfilment and variety that is hard to find elsewhere. You aren't just a doctor; you are a vital part of the community, enjoying access to the "great outdoors" right from your doorstep.

Learn more about healthcare careers in New Zealand: https://info.health.nz/careers/roles/senior-medical-officers/general-practitioners

KiwiRail and Team Global Express road-bridging operation

KiwiRail and Team Global Express kept freight moving while the Auckland rail network was closed for critical upgrades in January. Freight that would usually travel by train was trucked between Southdown in Auckland and Frankton and Hamilton Container Terminals.

Meet some of the team involved in this massive logistical operation.

KiwiRail's unsung heroes: James from Tito Group Limited

Meet James from TGL. James is part of the Wellington team installing cable to power up new safety signals, including barrier arms and automatic pedestrian gates at the level crossings. Outside work, James is pretty handy at cooking up a storm for the family.

Protect your place from Madagascar ragwort

Madagascar ragwort (Senecio madagascariensis) is a pasture weed that is rapidly spreading in Northland. It is likely to become the most serious threat to pastoral farming in New Zealand.   

Prevention, early detection and intervention is the best way to protect your farm or lifestyle block and reduce the impact of Madagascar ragwort on your farm and your neighbours'. 

For more information, visit www.nrc.govt.nz/MadagascarRagwort

Te Rūnanga Nui o Te Aupōuri  - Oranga Whenua Oranga Tangata Taiao - Kaitiakitanga

The Oranga Whenua Oranga Tangata Taiao team, through Te Runanga Nui O Te Aupouri's holistic approach, has achieved remarkable conservation outcomes. Their efforts include restoring native flora and fauna, enhancing wetlands and dune ecosystems, and fostering environmental awareness. They have installed more than 16,000 metres of fencing, planted 120,000 native plants, and captured over 2000 invasive pests. These achievements significantly contribute to the well-being of te taiao and strengthen connections between iwi and their whenua. The project exemplifies sustainable land management and community engagement in Te Taitokerau.

Winners of the Te Tohu Matua Supreme Award and Kaitiakitanga Award at Northland Regional Council's 2025 Whakamānawa ā Taiao – Environmental Awards. The Kaitiakitanga Award recognises the unique relationship tangata whenua have with natural and physical resources in accordance with tikanga Māori, and is open to whānau, hapū, iwi and Māori organisations.

Project Island Song - Environmental action to protect native life

Project Island Song has had a clear and lasting impact, with 15 years of pest-free status and 40,000 native trees planted. Their long-term commitment to restoring biodiversity in Pewhairangi Bay of Islands is remarkable. The group’s mahi supports native species by tackling pests, controlling weeds, and working to return lost wildlife. They collaborate with hapū, schools, families, individuals, and businesses, creating strong community partnerships. Their work with small, isolated schools is especially inspiring. With great measurable outcomes, this group is making a real difference for native life.

Winners of the Environmental action to protect native life Award at Northland Regional Council's 2025 Whakamānawa ā Taiao – Environmental Awards. This award recognises individuals or groups who are working to control pest animals, pest plants, and/or diseases to help our native life flourish.

Piroa Conservation Trust - Environmental action in water quality improvement

Piroa Conservation Trust comprises over 30 community-led conservation groups dedicated to restoring biodiversity in Bream Bay and surrounding areas. Since adding ‘Healthy Waterways’ to its vision in 2021, the Trust has delivered an impressive scope of initiatives with high community engagement. Their projects include riparian planting, water quality testing, wetland restoration, fencing, on-farm demonstrations, capability building, a native plant nursery, field days and community hui. Their strong relationships with iwi, hapū, and community groups, along with educational outreach and social media engagement, have raised awareness about water quality. They are also collaborating with Patuherekeke to incorporate mātauranga Māori into freshwater and biodiversity management. 

Winners of the Environmental action in water quality improvement Environmental Award at Northland Regional Council's 2025 Whakamānawa ā Taiao – Environmental Awards. This award recognises individuals or groups who are taking action to protect and enhance water quality and biodiversity values within water bodies in Northland.

Patuharakeke Te Iwi Trust - Te Pou Taiao - Environmental action to address climate change

e Pou Taiao o Patuharakake are leaders in supporting communities, whānau and marae to make informed decisions about climate change. They have developed an innovative climate change risk assessment toolbox to visually illustrate the risks to Patuharekeke rohe. The toolbox will be used to inform the Patuharakeke Hapū Environmental Management Plan, incorporating mātauranga Māori and western science within mitigation, adaptation and resilience strategies. Seamlessly integrating climate change considerations into all their activities, they are also leading impactful projects to benefit te taiao, including fish passage, fencing and planting Takahiwai Stream, Mediterranean fanworm removal, and a two-year survey of marine mammals in Bream Bay. 

Winners of the Environmental action to address climate change Award at Northland Regional Councils 2025 Whakamānawa ā Taiao – Environmental Awards. This award recognises individuals or groups who are taking action to adapt to a changing climate and transition to a low-carbon future for Northland.

KiwiRail and Team Global Express road-bridging operation

KiwiRail and Team Global Express kept freight moving while the Auckland rail network was closed for critical upgrades in January. Freight that would usually travel by train was trucked between Southdown in Auckland and Frankton and Hamilton Container Terminals.

KiwiRail's unsung heroes: James from Tito Group Limited

Te Kanapu Technical Approach Deep Dive webinar

Te Kanapu is Transpower's initiative to create a future grid blueprint for Aotearoa, to support economic growth and the drive for a net zero 2050.

As part of the development of the grid blueprint, Transpower published on 10 December 2025 a suite of documents outlining the technical approach they are using in this work.

This webinar, held on 12 February 2026, provided an opportunity for questions and answers diving into a variety of aspects of the technical approach and wider Te Kanapu programme..

You can read an executive summary of the technical approach, and access the full suite of documents, at www.transpower.co.nz/our-work/te-kanapu/technical-approach.

ASB Good as Gold: Anahera Hakiaha and Danielle Herewini

Anahera Hakiaha and Danielle Herewini of Whakatāne have created a run club to bring their community together and encourage healthy lifestyles. 

Celebrating their one-year anniversary, this club welcomes individuals of all running and walking abilities, including those who have never run before. The two women are incredibly supportive, always present, and dedicated to helping others. The club is completely free and voluntary, meeting 2-3 times a week with a schedule sent out every Sunday. They also introduce fun challenges to keep things interesting. Their motivation to start the club was simply to get and keep people moving. Beyond physical activity, the club offers a fantastic social experience, fostering connections among its members. 

ASB is thrilled to acknowledge Anahera and Danielle’s incredible initiative as this week’s ASB Good as Gold recipients.

ASB Good as Gold: Ben Prince-Saxon

This week’s ASB Good as Gold recipient is Ben Prince-Saxon. 

Ben has Cystic Fibrosis, a life-threatening genetic condition. In 2023, he began taking the pharmacy-funded drug Trikafta, and in 2024, he set an ambitious goal to run 12 marathons in 12 months to raise $25,000 for Cystic Fibrosis New Zealand. Through social media, speaking events, and interviews, he has been spreading awareness about CF while bringing people together to run alongside him in his marathons. Those who meet him describe him as humble, kind, thoughtful, and motivating. Before running his twelfth marathon, Ben had already raised $17,000 towards his goal. Running with lowered lung capacity, Ben’s efforts are nothing short of inspirational. Ben’s incredible journey is a testament to his strength and commitment to giving back to the community. 

ASB is honoured to recognise Ben’s extraordinary efforts with $10,000 as this week’s ASB Good as Gold recipient.

ASB Good as Gold: Ange Barker

This week’s ASB Good as Gold recipient is Ange Barker of Kerikeri. 

Back in 2019, a casual sideline chat sparked an idea: a safe, vibrant playground for kids at the Kerikeri Sports Complex. Ange took that seed and grew it into Te Amo Pūtoro – a unique space inspired by the four corners of local Māori heritage. Over six years she's navigated council hurdles, applied for countless grants, and rallied community support, all while juggling full-time work, study, and raising three boys with her husband Ben. Her determination never wavered, even when setbacks mounted. Today, Te Amo Pūtoro stands as Northland’s first playground of its kind – a testament to Ange’s vision, resilience, and ability to unite her community. 

ASB is proud to celebrate Ange’s extraordinary commitment with $10,000 as this week’s Good as Gold recipient.

ASB Good as Gold: Flow Waaka

This week’s ASB Good as Gold recipient is Flow Waaka of Christchurch. 

Initially featured on a segment on Seven Sharp, Flow’s inspirational work garnered nominations from Kiwis nationwide, leading to her recognition as an ASB Good as Gold recipient. Flow has been tirelessly feeding the homeless and low-income individuals twice a week for over a decade. Alongside her dedicated team, she prepares and serves meals, and provides essential items like gloves, beanies, socks, blankets, and sleeping bags. She utilizes her social media platforms to raise awareness, funds, and to seek assistance. Her charitable efforts have even helped two individuals acquire cars. Flow is celebrated for her respect, passion, kindness, selflessness, and unwavering commitment. 

ASB is honoured to acknowledge Flow Waaka’s remarkable contributions with $10,000 as this week’s ASB Good as Gold recipient.

ASB Good as Gold: Jim Little

This week’s ASB Good as Gold recipient is Jim Little of Christchurch. 

Jim has dedicated over 60 years to rowing; coaching numerous schools, young rowers, NZ Junior crews, and a number of masters rowers. Through his entire rowing career, he has remained loyal to the Union Rowing Club. Jim's contributions extend beyond coaching. He has towed and repaired boats, painted oars, helped construct a new rowing shed, and operated safety boats at regattas. Now in his 80s, Jim continues to share his extensive knowledge and passion with rowers of all ages and backgrounds, without seeking recognition or payment. His impact on the community is immense, inspiring countless individuals to enhance their skills and confidence. His dedication, loyalty, resilience, and wisdom make him an outstanding mentor and role model. With his unwavering commitment to both the sport and its people, Jim continues to make a significant difference.

 ASB is honoured to recognise Jim's remarkable contributions with $10,000 as this week’s ASB Good as Gold recipient.

ASB Good as Gold: Betty-May

This week’s ASB Good as Gold recipient is Betty-May of Tairua. 

A powerhouse of community spirit, Betty-May founded a new league club for local tamariki, with the Tairua Taniwha's now home to over 70 players. She secures sponsors for uniforms, sources first aid kits and training gear, and makes sure every team have what they need. Beyond the field, she volunteers at Tairua School, sharing her passion for kapa haka and te reo Māori, and leads regular waiata sessions that bring the community together. All this, while running a busy takeaway shop and raising a family. 

ASB is honoured to celebrate Betty-May’s tireless dedication and aroha with $10,000 as this week’s ASB Good as Gold recipient.
